text:
Jacob Trouba is on his fourth NHL team, a former Rangers captain now playing 22 minutes a night as the veteran presence on a young San Jose blue line. The Sharks also seem to enjoy his life away from the rink: San Jose Hockey Now had him talking art this week, and the team gave him an episode of its Undercurrent series.

On the ice, he's doing what Trouba does: 41 hits, 35 blocks and 10 points in 22 games, though he's pointless in six straight and our form check says the chances have thinned out too. The good news is relative. San Jose takes only 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, but that's three points better than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him below replacement level last season in Anaheim, and NHL Edge puts his top speed in the 9th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows the trade-off: he stops 16% of the entries aimed at him, well above typical, but only 28% of his exits keep possession. He's a defender who holds the line and then too often gives the puck back.
